'''Ōkume no Mikoto''' (大久米命) is a legendary figure from ancient {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan}}, recorded in texts such as the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} and {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}. He is revered as the ancestor of the {{ill|Kumebe|ja|久米直}} clan, a prominent ancient warrior lineage. The ''Nihon Shoki'' sometimes refers to him as "Ōkume" (大来目).

== Genealogy ==
According to the ''Kojiki'', Ōkume no Mikoto joined the {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|en|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|qid=Q11590444|lt=Eastern Expedition}} of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|qid=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}}, alongside {{ill|Michinoomi|ja|道臣命}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|en|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|qid=Q17227938|lt=Ōtomo clan}}). Together, they defeated local chieftains such as {{ill|Eukashi|ja|兄猾}}, the {{ill|Tsuchigumo|en|Tsuchigumo|qid=Q2063089|lt=Tsuchigumo}} lord {{ill|Yasotakeru|ja|八十梟帥}}, and other o11onents in the {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}}.<ref name="jimmu">''Kojiki'', middle volume, Emperor Jimmu section.</ref> His actions are celebrated in the ''Nihon Shoki'', which notes the singing of {{ill|Kume no Uta|ja|久米歌}}, martial songs to inspire warriors during battle.<ref>''Nihon Shoki'', Emperor Jimmu pre-enthronement, year戊午, 10th month, 2nd day.</ref>

The ''Kojiki'' identifies Ōkume no Mikoto’s ancestor as {{ill|Amanokume no Mikoto|ja|天津久米命}},<ref>''Kojiki'', u11er volume, Tenson Ninigi section.</ref> while the ''Nihon Shoki'' refers to him as "Ame Kushitsu Ōkume" (天槵津大来目). Both sources agree on their role as protectors of the {{ill|Posterity of Heaven|ja|天孫|ko|천손|qid=Q108278353}}, indicating a long-standing military tradition.

== Legacy ==
In the ''Kojiki'', Ōkume no Mikoto is depicted as an equal partner to Michinoomi no Mikoto in leading Emperor Jimmu's forces. However, in the ''Nihon Shoki'', Ōkume is portrayed as subordinate, suggesting that the Kumebe clan's influence declined over time, with leadership passing to the Ōtomo clan.

The ''Kojiki'' also records Ōkume’s role in arranging Emperor Jimmu’s marriage to {{ill|Himetataraisuzu-hime|ja|伊須気余理比売}}. During the courtship, Ōkume performed a {{ill|sedōka|ja|旋頭歌|fr|Sedōka|it|Sedōka|hu|Szedóka|pl|Sedōka|hi|सेदोका|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sedōka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q678489}} that refers to "tattooed eyes," implying he may have worn traditional warrior tattoos.<ref name="jimmu" />
